scope: Independent local source/AST and existing CPU inspection review of one isolated diagnostic adapter. No GPU/model/DT/backward/update or remote call was performed by this review; no production file was edited.
verdict: No concrete loss duplication, wrong saved-Q field, native-mask/denominator change, asymmetric-rank support skipping, or missing wrapper restoration was found in the reviewed sources. This is source/CPU interface evidence, not runtime gradient values, numerical tolerance evidence, or proof of unchanged model parameters after execution.

verified_CPU_inspection.existing_cloudpickle_identity_inspection: verify.inspect_inputs uses identity of deserialized original worker method; the existing CPU invocation completed these assertions.
verified_CPU_inspection.new_local_execution: Only stdlib source/receipt parsing and embedded-Python AST parsing; no fake tensors or model/optimizer runtime.

source_contracts.finding: Selection is literally dt_q_estimates != 0 or == 0. Official _snapshot creates a separate TensorDict container; only diagnostic_grpo_advantages is rebound through torch.where. No renormalization or support-dependent mask/denominator is introduced.

Only label grpo_pg invokes _grpo_snapshot to bind saved diagnostic_GRPO into advantages; dt_pg passes the unchanged complete DT data. The two support calls therefore repeat the same DT branch for comparison, not two disjoint DT support gradients.

NativeLossHooks calls the actual original policy_loss/agg_loss objects and returns those objects. Hooks select scalar upstream backward gradients; no PPO/GRPO loss or token reduction is implemented by the new adapter. The original class.update_policy is invoked, bypassing only the temporary instance diagnostic wrapper.

The original observer requires local32, B4, one epoch and static vanilla path. The native clip executes through the saved original _optimizer_step; only optimizer.step is temporarily no-op. Full original loss_mask and B4/8 denominator remain. Snapshot is taken before native clip, so gradient statistics remain pre-clip.

Temporary LABELS, actor.update_policy, worker scheduler.step, optimizer.step, actor._optimizer_step and native scalar hooks restore in finally/context exits. Original observer restores saved gradient objects/contents, module training flags and gradient_accumulation; fork_rng and explicit Python/NumPy restoration preserve caller RNG. No optimizer or scheduler implementation is copied.

Each DP rank receives one local32 partition; driver loops q_nonzero then q_zero on both ranks. Each loops dt_pg then grpo_pg unconditionally. There is no early return for an empty local support. Expected workload is 4 complete local32 passes/rank, each 8 original B4 backwards: 32 primitive microbatch backward calls/rank, 4 native clip boundaries/rank, 2 no-op scheduler calls/rank. This count describes planned source behavior, not a newly observed GPU result.

One official worker group, one init_model and one complete checkpoint25 load precede both support calls. Real Adam observer imported by recipe is never called; no rollout or DT is invoked. Params are intended to remain unchanged via optimizer no-op; this review does not invent a runtime equality gate.

Composes guarded existing SCRIPT, verifies exact saved input/native dependency/owner bytes, CPU inspection, and prepared-to-launch source/input/config/checkpoint equality; it adds no training or environment implementation. The completed CPU prepare binds actor 1f862e8b, worker e5eb4afc and core fc2f992b.

scope_cautions: Support counts include every tensor position, including padding. q_zero support is not a count of failed trajectories or valid action tokens; actual gradients use the original full mask.

Four backward passes means four complete local32 accumulated passes per rank, not four B4 backward calls. Existing original helper scope contains a generic four-pass text inherited under temporary LABELS=2; adapter overwrites scope and records actual_backward_passes from passes. original_observer_scope should not be used as the new per-support runtime count.

Scalar hooks suppress upstream gradients only; original entropy/KL/nonselected backward bodies still execute. Zero upstream gradients do not erase nonfinite intermediates. No new masking or alternate kernel semantics are inferred.
Saved official global-UID normalized GRPO coefficients are a diagnostic comparator, not oracle advantages or a proposed replacement for DT Q/V/A.
CPU equality/source/serialization checks do not prove model numerical tolerance, runtime gradient equality, optimizer-state immutability, or historical learning quality.
